constraints: Preserve the behavior the application depends on, and check each Vue 2 behavior listed in the Vue 3 breaking changes against the reported files.
Keep a single Vue runtime in the build: when the project uses vue-template-compiler, replace it with @vue/compiler-sfc.

steps.instructions: Upgrade straight to Vue 3, or install @vue/compat at the same version as vue and alias vue to it to run Vue 2 compatible behavior first. vue-cli projects can run vue upgrade to update @vue/cli-service.
steps.title: Choose the upgrade path

steps.instructions: Set vue to a 3.x version in dependencies, and replace vue-template-compiler with @vue/compiler-sfc in devDependencies when present. Custom webpack setups upgrade vue-loader to ^16.0.0.
steps.title: Update the Vue dependencies

steps.instructions: At each reported import, replace new Vue() root instances with createApp() and move global configuration onto the application instance.
steps.title: Replace the Vue 2 global API

steps.instructions: Build and run the application, fix each compatibility warning until none remain, then remove @vue/compat and switch the compiler to Vue 3 mode.
steps.title: Clear migration build warnings

verification.purpose: Confirm that one Vue 3 release resolves and no Vue 2 copy remains.
Compile the application and surface any remaining compiler warnings.
Run the repository tests when defined.

rule.replacement: Vue 3 (vue@^3), following the Vue 3 migration guide
rule.summary: Vue 2 has reached end of life and is no longer actively maintained. After December 31st, 2023 it receives no updates, including security and browser compatibility fixes.
rule.title: Vue 2 is end-of-life
